All tests pass.

## Root cause
`app/intervals.py` contained a stub: `merge_intervals` just did `return list(intervals)`, so it never merged anything. The visible test `merge_intervals([(1, 3), (2, 4)]) == [(1, 4)]` failed because the input was returned unchanged.

## Fix
Rewrote `merge_intervals` in **`app/intervals.py`** (only file changed; nothing under `tests/` touched):
- Sorts intervals by `(start, end)` so unsorted input works.
- Merges when the next interval starts at or before the current end (`start <= last_end`), which also handles touching intervals like `(1,2),(2,3)`.
- Handles empty input, single intervals, fully nested intervals, and disjoint intervals.
- Preserves the input element type (tuples in → tuples out, lists in → lists out) and never mutates the caller's data.

## Test command
```
/usr/local/py-utils/bin/pytest -q
```
Result: `1 passed`. (Note: the default `python` on PATH has no pytest installed, so I used the pytest venv interpreter — equivalently `/usr/local/py-utils/venvs/pytest/bin/python -m pytest -q`, which also reports `1 passed`.)

I also spot-checked edge cases manually: empty list, single interval, nested `(1,4),(2,3)`, disjoint `(1,2),(3,4)`, touching `(1,2),(2,3)`, unsorted input, and list-of-lists input — all produce correct merged output.
